subject: Post-demo: lift-and-shift readiness & next steps
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T16:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: lift-and-shift readiness & next steps

Hi Samir — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope a clean pilot: 

Summary of what I heard
- Primary product: conversational insights and document summarization for financial analyst workflows.
- Current infra: self-hosted model serving on an on-prem GPU cluster (Slurm-based), plus separate batch inference pipelines for nightly processing.
- Key constraints: sensitive PII in some inputs, procurement wants a predictable cost model, and latency requirement for the analyst-facing UI is ~200ms p95.

Open questions for scoping the pilot
1) Traffic profile: can you share typical QPS for interactive vs batch (ballpark numbers are fine)?
2) Data residency: do any datasets need to remain entirely on-prem / air-gapped?
3) Network/topology: would you be able to establish VPN or VPC peering for a Dedicated pilot, or is Private (VPC/on-prem) the only viable path?
4) Migration window: do you need a lift-and-shift cutover or are you open to a dual-run (shadow traffic) approach for 2–4 weeks?

Proposed next steps
- If you're open, schedule a 45-minute ops/infra call (we'll bring an engineer) to validate network/SLAs and get the Slurm cluster details.
- We'll prepare two pilot options: (A) Dedicated Reserved pool with VPN peering + monitoring, (B) Private VPC deployment with customer-managed control plane — include an estimated timeline and cost delta.

I attached a short checklist we use for these lift-and-shift pilots and a link to the Dedicated vs Private comparison doc. If you can reply with answers to the 4 questions above (or attach any network diagrams), I'll assemble a draft pilot SOW.

Thanks — looking forward to the ops call.

Best,
Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Pilot_Checklist.pdf (pdf)]
From: Samir Kapoor <samir@finlytics.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-team@finlytics.com
Date: 2027-05-18T18:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: lift-and-shift readiness & next steps

Ava — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers below and a file attached (security questionnaire).

Answers to your questions
1) Traffic: interactive is small today — ~6 qps during business hours (spiky), batch jobs run nightly and produce embeddings for ~2 million docs over an 8 hour window.
2) Data residency: customer PII (names, account numbers) must stay in the EU for a subset of customers; however the analyst-facing product currently operates in the US. We may need a hybrid where EU traffic stays in-region.
3) Network/topology: procurement has strong controls; VPN peering to a Dedicated environment is possible but needs an approved IP allowlist and a SOC2 report. Full on-prem air-gapped Private is a harder sell but not impossible for compliance customers.
4) Migration window: prefer a dual-run approach. We can't risk a straight cutover from the Slurm cluster.

Notes on the Slurm cluster
- Old CUDA drivers on a few nodes; ops is concerned about kernel compat.
- Custom batching glue we've built for throughput.

I've attached our security QA PDF (FinLytics_Security_QA.pdf). Let's get the ops call on the calendar — please include someone from Redwood who can speak to VPN peering and required reports for procurement.

—Samir
Samir Kapoor
Head of Product
FinLytics
[Attachment: FinLytics_Security_QA.pdf (pdf)]
From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T19:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: lift-and-shift readiness & next steps

Samir — perfect visibility, thanks. A few follow-ups and a short proposal for the ops call: 

Follow-ups
- We'll bring an infra engineer who can answer VPN peering, SOC2 scope, and pilot network requirements.
- We'll also bring a runtime engineer to talk about how we handle kernel/CUDA mismatches and options for a short-term compatibility layer.

Pilot proposal (high level)
- Phase 0 (validation): quick infra questionnaire + VPN smoke test (1 week).
- Phase 1 (Dedicated pilot): Reserved Dedicated pool in us-west with VPN peering, shadow traffic for 2 weeks, token-level cost/latency traces.
- Phase 2 (Optional Private cutover): If procurement requires, plan Private VPC with customer-managed control plane and HSM/KMS integration.

Attached is a basic diagram of how we typically route traffic during a lift-and-shift pilot — this will help ops map to your Slurm cluster. If you give the go-ahead we'll propose two SOW options (Dedicated-first vs Private-first) and an estimated timeline and cost.

When are you available for the ops call? I'm free tomorrow between 10–12 PST or Friday morning.

Thanks,
Ava
[Attachment: diagram_legacy_infra.png (png)]
From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: lift-and-shift readiness & next steps — FinLytics (heads-up)

Aditya / Marissa — forwarding the thread with FinLytics (deal DL-2027-FIN-09). Key points and risk profile: 

- FinLytics runs an older on-prem Slurm cluster with custom batching; will need runtime engineering time to validate compatibility.
- They require SOC2 evidence for Dedicated VPN peering; EU data residency requirement adds complexity.
- Preferred approach: Dedicated pilot with VPN peering and shadow traffic, then evaluate Private VPC for EU workloads or procurement demands.

Suggested internal actions
1) Prioritize a runtime engineer for a 1-hour deep-dive on CUDA/kernel compatibility.
2) Pre-prepare SOC2 + procurement packet and a Private VPC checklist.
3) Draft two SOW templates (Dedicated-first, Private-first) and estimated costs.

I'll set up the ops call once Samir confirms a time. Happy to take point on the pilot SOW drafts.

Ava
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
